method.tool: scratchpad/tools/coverage_search.py (--regex --whole-words), seven term sets in search/C12/terms.txt (S1-day to S7-happy); S8 has no term file and was judged from records and Doc_05; record check by recgrep.py -> recgrep.json; hand reads of front matter
method.record_check: independent front-matter grep (recgrep.py) plus reading each cited record with show2.py
method.verification: verify.py (copied from search/C3): quote text normalised and searched in the vendored file named by the source record; five misses were read by hand and are editorial artifacts (marginal letters, footnote marks, an italic tag), not wording changes
method.layers: RENDERED = a record speaks to the sub-question (R* = partial or guard only); LOADED = vendored and mapped, read in context, no record; IDENTIFIED = registered unvendored source (kind: unvendored); OTHER = outside the repo; NOTHING = none found. The tool scans whole mapped files, so loci were chosen by hand.

gallic.doc05: Doc_05 sec 1.2 (dress, food, sleep, cell, labour, climate, sexuality) is the richest daily-life text in the fleet: camel-hair at Marmoutier, winter hoods, five fast days a week, no sleep after the night office, caves and one wooden cell, copying as the only craft. Only lentils, weekly service and clothes became records. It also logs three excised body/sexuality texts in the English Cassian.

S1.note: Strict house, shared duties, circus as ruin's cure. Meals, sleep and fasts from Doc_05 are not records.

S2.note: Dress and the cell. Cassian describes Egypt, not Gaul (not_for).

S3.note: About two thousand monks at Martin's funeral; work by turns. Letters and travel not covered.

S4.note: Fever at deaths only. Sulpicius L4932 "plague" is hail, not disease.

S5.note: Martin's funeral and Salvian's unburied dead of Trier.

S6.note: Leaving the army; renunciation. Distance not covered.

S7.note: Cassian's goal (purity of heart) and end (the kingdom) answer "the point" directly.

S8.note: Honest limit for caves, cell and island.

witt.doc05: Doc_05 sec 1.2 (rising, work, table, bed, food, sex, sickness, death) is the second-richest daily-life text: morning and evening blessings (SC 543-607), meat and fast-day liberty, the calamity list with pestilence and cattle-plague (LC 3507), the churchyard as "resting place" (Hy 957-1019). Records carry the household, daily rhythm, fasting and death; the blessings and calamity list are not records.
